drills.title: Forcible Entry Size-Up & Tool Selection
drills.goal: Read the access problem, select appropriate tools and communicate a controlled entry plan before forcing an approved prop.
objectives: Select tools based on the problem
State a backup plan before committing
setup: Use only approved training props or tabletop/photo problems
Inspect tools and establish striking/cutting safety zones
Prepare multiple access problems without naming the solution
evolution: Crew sizes up construction and selects tools
Crew states primary and backup plan
Perform approved technique or verbalize it when no prop is available
Rotate roles and change the problem
performance: Crew recognizes when the initial plan is ineffective and changes tactics
criticalErrors: Using a live building or unapproved prop
drills.remediation: Return to tabletop size-up and tool identification before a slow coached prop evolution.
drills.advanced: Combine access problem with smoke/fire information requiring the crew to balance speed, control and alternate entry.
aar: What construction clue drove your tool choice?
What was your backup plan?
Where was the highest injury risk?
When should you abandon the first technique?
drills.outcome: Crew approaches forcible entry as a size-up and decision problem rather than a memorized tool sequence.

drills.title: Hose Kinks, Stream Quality & Flow Recognition
drills.goal: Connect hose layout and restrictions to stream quality and delivered fire flow.
setup: Establish a safe flowing-water area
Set department-approved pump/nozzle conditions
Record baseline flow when a flowmeter is available
evolution: Instructor introduces a controlled hose-layout restriction
Nozzle member describes the change without initially seeing the hose
Backup/crew locates and corrects the problem
performance: Crew connects hose management to water delivery
drills.remediation: Compare baseline and one obvious restriction side-by-side before repeating without coaching.
drills.advanced: Integrate operator pressure/flow observations and FireOps Calc hydraulics discussion.
aar: What changed at the nozzle?
Which restriction was hardest to recognize?
What should nozzle and operator communicate?
How can deployment prevent the problem?
drills.outcome: Crew recognizes and corrects hose-layout problems before they materially undermine attack performance.

drills.title: Flow Path, Door Control & Coordinated Ventilation
drills.goal: Predict how openings and suppression actions can alter the fire environment and coordinate ventilation with fire attack.
setup: Use a non-live-fire visual prop or FireOpsSim scenario unless qualified live-fire resources are separately provided
Prepare several opening configurations
Identify suppression position and victim/search information
evolution: Add suppression/search assignment and require coordinated action plan
performance: Members explain why an opening matters
Ventilation is treated as coordinated tactical action
criticalErrors: Applying tabletop conclusions as universal rules without considering local conditions
drills.remediation: Use a single-room diagram with one inlet/outlet before adding multiple openings.
drills.advanced: Run three roles—suppression, search and ventilation—with separate information and radio coordination.
aar: What established the likely flow path?
What changed when the opening changed?
When should ventilation occur?
What information must crews exchange?
drills.outcome: Members reason from conditions and coordinate actions that alter the fire environment.
sources: FSRI coordinated attack and fire dynamics training

drills.title: RIT/RIC Firefighter Location, Packaging & Removal
drills.goal: Organize a controlled rescue of a down firefighter from location through packaging and removal while preserving crew accountability and air awareness.
objectives: Package and move using approved techniques
setup: Use a safe non-IDLH training area
Place mannequin and establish stop signal
Stage only department-approved rescue equipment
evolution: Provide Mayday information to rescue team
Package and move to designated safe area
performance: Rescue problem is assessed before uncontrolled movement
Removal technique matches environment and staffing
drills.remediation: Practice packaging/removal on open floor before adding search and radio components.
drills.advanced: Integrate Mayday command, separate rescue group supervisor and EMS handoff.
aar: What information helped locate the firefighter?
What slowed packaging?
When was additional help needed?
How was team air/accountability managed?
drills.outcome: RIT/RIC members execute a rehearsed rescue process rather than improvising under pressure.

drills.title: Apparatus Placement Decision Tabletop
drills.goal: Position first- and later-arriving apparatus to support incident objectives while preserving access, water supply and escape routes.
setup: Choose actual district locations or representative maps
Identify hydrants, overhead hazards and access limits
Prepare first-due and later-arriving resource cards
evolution: Show incident location and initial conditions
Reveal one access or water complication
criticalErrors: Placement knowingly traps apparatus in scenario
drills.remediation: Use one engine and one hydrant problem before adding multiple resources.
drills.advanced: Run a full first-alarm placement exercise with command assigning functions after units commit.
aar: What did you preserve for later companies?
Could the apparatus leave if conditions worsened?
How did water supply affect placement?
What local address deserves a preplan?
drills.outcome: Drivers and officers place apparatus based on the whole incident rather than only proximity to the address.

drills.title: Aerial Positioning & Scrub-Area Decision Drill
equipment: aerial apparatus or tabletop apparatus template
drills.goal: Select a safe aerial position that supports the stated objective within apparatus/manufacturer limitations.
objectives: Consider scrub area and stabilization footprint
setup: Use actual apparatus only in an approved training area; otherwise use tabletop maps
Have manufacturer limits available
Choose several target points
evolution: Change target or block preferred position
drills.remediation: Perform tabletop spotting with apparatus footprint before any apparatus movement.
drills.advanced: Coordinate aerial and engine placement for a commercial incident.
aar: What was the objective before spotting?
What limited scrub area?
What did your position block?
What alternate position remains viable?
drills.outcome: Crew treats aerial placement as an objective-driven positioning problem within equipment limits.

drills.title: WUI Structure Triage & Go/No-Go Decision
drills.goal: Assess whether structure-protection operations can be conducted safely while considering fire behavior, access/egress, fuels, hazards and water supply.
objectives: Choose an engagement or disengagement plan
setup: Use tabletop/photos unless operating under qualified wildland instructors
Provide wind/fire-spread information
Mark access, turnarounds and water sources
evolution: State whether and how to engage
Reveal worsening fire behavior or blocked route
performance: Decision changes when conditions exceed capability
criticalErrors: Plan depends on an escape route declared unusable
Commits resources to instructor-declared non-defensible conditions
drills.remediation: Use two clearly contrasting defensible/non-defensible examples before ambiguous cases.
drills.advanced: Triage several structures and prioritize limited engine resources.
aar: What made the structure defendable or not?
Could the engine leave quickly?
How long would water last?
What change would trigger disengagement?
drills.outcome: Crew performs repeatable WUI risk analysis and recognizes when structure protection should not be attempted.
sources: NWCG S-215 Fire Operations in WUI

drills.title: HazMat First-Due Recognition, Isolation & Information
drills.goal: Recognize a potential hazardous-materials incident, avoid premature commitment and communicate the information needed for an appropriate response.
objectives: Approach from a safer position based on available information
Communicate observations without guessing product identity
setup: Use photos/tabletop only unless qualified HazMat training resources are provided
Prepare occupancy, placard and container clues
Use current department-approved reference materials
evolution: Identify clues from a safe simulated distance
Use approved reference to frame initial actions
Request appropriate resources and give concise report
performance: Crew does not rush into unknown hazard
criticalErrors: Simulated entry into unknown release without appropriate capability
Treating placard/reference lookup as definitive field identification
drills.remediation: Return to recognition-only photo cards and practice describing what is actually observed.
drills.advanced: Add command transfer to HazMat group and changing weather information.
aar: What clue first changed your approach?
What did you know versus assume?
Where would you stage?
What specialist/resource is needed next?
drills.outcome: First-due crew recognizes HazMat cues, limits exposure and initiates a disciplined information/resource process.
sources: Department HazMat SOP/SOG and current ERG

drills.title: SCBA Radio Communications Under Workload
drills.goal: Maintain understandable, concise radio communication while wearing the department's SCBA and performing controlled work.
objectives: Recognize equipment/accessory limitations before IDLH use
setup: Use the same make/model equipment members use operationally
Inspect radio/SCBA accessory configuration
Use moderate controlled workload and clear stop criteria
evolution: Member sends baseline message without SCBA
Perform controlled task then transmit assignment/progress message
performance: Member recognizes communication failure and uses local backup procedure
criticalErrors: Assuming accessory performance without department validation
drills.remediation: Practice stationary radio manipulation in full PPE before adding workload.
drills.advanced: Run command plus two crews with controlled radio traffic and Mayday-channel transition discussion.
aar: What changed with SCBA/PPE?
Which controls were difficult?
How did workload affect speech?
What is the backup if the accessory fails?
drills.outcome: Members can communicate reliably in their operational PPE/SCBA configuration and understand its limitations.

drills.title: Coordinated Attack: Suppression, Search & Ventilation
drills.goal: Coordinate separate company objectives so suppression, search and ventilation actions support rather than undermine one another.
objectives: Share conditions and intent between companies
Sequence actions that alter fire conditions
setup: Assign command, suppression, search and ventilation roles
Give each role different but overlapping information
Use simulation/tabletop unless qualified practical-training resources are provided
evolution: Instructor reveals changed conditions based on coordination
Command updates plan and crews complete AAR
performance: Ventilation is coordinated rather than automatic
criticalErrors: Independent action ignores known effect on another crew
Command fails to react to declared deteriorating condition
drills.remediation: Run suppression plus one other function before restoring all roles.
drills.advanced: Use separate rooms/phones/radios so members only receive information that is actually communicated.
aar: Which information was trapped within one crew?
Did any action surprise another company?
What should command have known sooner?
What communication changed the outcome?
drills.outcome: Members experience coordinated fireground operations as an information and timing problem, not independent task completion.
sources: FSRI Coordination of Suppression and Ventilation
